faqs.a: A practical subset: lists of records, single records, nested maps, quoted strings, numbers, booleans, nulls and comments. Anchors, aliases, tags and multi-line block scalars (| and >) are not supported and will show a parse error.
Yes. In YAML output, nested objects become indented maps and arrays become dash lists. In CSV and XML output, nested values are written as compact JSON text inside the cell or element.
Yes. Names are sanitized into valid XML names, special characters are escaped, and an XML declaration with UTF-8 encoding is included.
Both directions are first-class. The swap button flips the formats and converts the current output back into the input box, so round-trips are one click.
faqs.q: Can I convert back and forth?

faqs.a: The XML reader treats the root's child elements as records and their children as fields. Attributes are ignored; if you need attribute support, use the JSON, XML & CSV converter.

json-to-yaml.formula: records = parse(input, from)  →  output = emit(records, to)
howTo: Choose the input format: JSON, YAML, XML or CSV.
Choose the output format, or press Swap to flip the direction.
Paste your data, or press Sample for an example in the input format.
Set the CSV delimiter or XML element names if those options appear.
Press Download to save the converted file, or Copy to paste it elsewhere.
keyFacts: Converts between JSON, YAML, XML and CSV in any direction on one page.
YAML support covers lists of records, nested maps, quoted strings, numbers, booleans, nulls and comments.
XML input reads child elements as records; XML output is well-formed with customizable element names.
CSV parsing and emission handle quoting, escaped quotes and line breaks.
Invalid input shows a friendly error instead of crashing.

labels.yamlNote: YAML support is a practical subset: records, nested maps, quoted strings, numbers, booleans, nulls and comments. Anchors and block scalars are not supported.

limitations: YAML anchors, aliases, tags and multi-line block scalars are not supported.
XML attributes are ignored when reading XML input.
Nested values become JSON text in CSV and XML output, not expanded structures.
Very large inputs (tens of MB) can make the browser tab sluggish.

json-to-yaml.workedExample:
JSON to YAML input:
[{"name":"Aarav Sharma","age":25}]

YAML output:
- name: Aarav Sharma
  age: 25

1 record, 2 fields.

YAML to CSV input:
- name: Aarav Sharma
  age: 25
- name: Priya Verma
  age: 30

CSV output:
name,age
Aarav Sharma,25
Priya Verma,30

2 records, 2 fields.
